## Server and client runtimes

Keep separate composition:

- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.

Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.

Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.

For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
Effect fibre without another runtime.

Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Loaders and actions

Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:

1. decode params/search/body/session;
2. call a named Effect service operation;
3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
4. encode hydration-safe data;
5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.

Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.

## TanStack Query

Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.

Define intentionally:

- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
- invalidation after mutation;
- server prefetch/hydration encoding.

Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.

## TanStack Router/Start

Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.

For serialisable loader data:

- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
- prove all error variants are handled.

Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
transport, including an error response status.

### Router preloading and freshness

Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
page can render immediately while a return starts another API GET
request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.

For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.

Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
separate owners. An API reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.

Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.

## Initial JavaScript and fonts

Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
## React lifecycle

For subscriptions/streams:

- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
- scope to mount/route lifetime;
- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
- encode backpressure/sampling;
- update view state through a controlled adapter.

Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.

When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
An optional registration/subscription pattern is
`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
not required for purely synchronous local UI state.

Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
state or cleanup has a real owner.

Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.

Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.

## State

Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.

Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.

## Errors

Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:

- not found;
- unauthorised;
- validation fields;
- unavailable/retry;
- conflict;
- unexpected defect boundary.

Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.

## Tests

Test:

- domain service independently;
- loader/action decoding and encoding;
- runtime bridge and cancellation;
- hydration round-trip;
- retry ownership;
- subscription cleanup;
- no server dependency in client bundle;
- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
  a stalled unrelated service;
- exhaustive UI error states.

## Native public HTTP reads for a separate Website and API

```text
first request -> Website server loader -> one server runner
              -> HttpApiClient.make -> private same-stage BACKEND -> API
navigation/preload -> same loader's client branch -> shared Atom registry
              -> AtomHttpApi.Service client -> public API GET -> domain
component reactive read -> native ApiClient.query -> same registry/client
local setup -> checked Website bindings/cookie -> retained local atoms
```

Choose the transport from the required behaviour. Public reads that need CDN
caching use native `HttpApi` GET endpoints and their generated clients. Native
RPC remains a deliberate option for procedure/streaming requirements; ordinary
POST RPC results do not become cacheable public GETs by enabling Worker caching.
Use shared domain Schemas in the native endpoint contract. Do not copy Content
or Training into replica client services that only rename generated calls.

`createIsomorphicFn().server(...).client(...)` selects local code without
creating a Website endpoint. Server reads use native `HttpApiClient.make` over
Alchemy's public `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` binding conversion.
Browser reads use checked public API configuration and credential-free native
FetchHttpClient. The native 4.0.2 Layer uses HttpClient.layerMergedContext to
retain provided RequestInit options for execution. Use that existing Layer and
test actual outgoing options; do not add a policy wrapper without a demonstrated
requirement. Do not add `createServerFn`, a Website proxy, or backend routes
merely to read that API. Keep runtime imports in matching environment branches.

Native `AtomHttpApi.Service` accepts `runtime: browserRuntime.factory`; native
service runtimes then share the application factory and router/React registry.
The default factory is not a reason to forbid the native Service. Do not start
another application runner, registry or copied client lifecycle. Create one
browser registry before loaders run, provide that exact registry to React, and
close it at final unmount. The portable ownership rule allows AtomRegistry.make
only inside createLoaderRegistry at the configured browser owner. Isolated test
registries require exact registryTests paths ending in .test/.spec.ts or .tsx;
glob paths, another test file and production files do not gain permission.
Aliases and exported constructor references remain checked. Preserve development replay and pending-request
cleanup tests. SSR registries are isolated; no mutable module-global registry.

Use `baseUrl` when the checked API origin is fixed during construction. When
root configuration is retained in an Atom, use the native `httpClient(get)`
composition callback and native request mapping to read it. This callback is a
native configuration hook, not an owned Layer factory. Keep configuration atoms
alive for the registry lifetime and check configuration before client acquisition
when its named error must remain distinct. Local appearance/progress must not
wait on remote clients or an unrelated optional service.

TanStack owns route loading, preloading, freshness and serialisation. Loader-only
reads call the generated client directly; the sole browser Promise bridge runs
that request Effect using the same registry. Do not create a `pageLoaderAtom`
or another query cache for every route. Components owning reactive remote state
use native `ApiClient.query`; tools and loaders that need typed operational
errors can call the native client directly. In Effect 4.0.2 native query helpers
turn Schema/HttpClient failures into defects; test the actual path rather than
claiming every helper keeps those errors in its typed channel.

Keep failures typed inside Effect and translate once at the framework boundary
to native TanStack not-found/error handling. Plain successful values use native
TanStack serialisation. Convert only values requiring an explicit checked view;
do not add success/error envelopes, reply codecs or repeated Schema decoding
solely to serialise a plain successful result. A format-selected response still
needs one semantic variant check before promising a narrower type; its callers
must reuse that narrowing. Reuse API-owned finished downloads through a single
native binding request instead of refetching data and rebuilding the response.

Wrap the complete native call in `Effect.timeout` when the product needs a
request deadline. The operation includes body reading and Schema decoding.
In the qualified HttpClient, `transformResponse` surrounds response acquisition
(headers); in HttpApiClient/AtomHttpApi it surrounds body decoding after headers
have arrived. Timing either stage alone misses part of the complete request.
Choose the duration for the feature; ten or forty seconds are examples, not
framework requirements. Preserve earlier caller interruption, response cleanup,
native tagged errors and unrelated defects. Test late headers then a stalled
body with TestClock, invalid JSON/schema replies and final registry disposal.

Review every owned helper with the deletion test: would deleting it remove
complexity, or force meaningful policy into several callers? Delete pass-through
Layers/services/hooks, generic request factories, duplicated error conversions
and wrappers around native defaults. Keep checked host adapters, real feature
policy and one required runner. Local lint/build proof does not establish hosted
CORS, direct browser GETs, private binding startup or cache hits.

See the Alchemy [native public caching guide](../../../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md#native-public-response-caching)
for response eligibility, version isolation and hosted cache evidence.

Use the portable [native request ownership checks](../enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
to reject recognised loader request state, generated-client replica services,
duplicate checked replies and Website data proxies. Configure real import and
owner paths and prove both valid native patterns and forbidden replacements
with the actual Oxlint command. Their local syntax coverage does not replace

With a key, it calls `toRpcAsync<typeof TaxKitApiWorker>(binding).calculatorRequest(incoming, NetAddress.formatIp(key))`. The comment at `:60-62` says the native RPC cannot carry an AbortSignal, so cancelling the call does not stop remote work.

+Cooper agreed on 10 October 2026 that both the standalone Bun API and the
+Cloudflare API remain supported. Shared calculation and transport packages must
+work without knowing which host runs them. Each app host supplies its server,
+configuration and platform services to the same checked operations.
+Cloudflare setup is the priority. Bun remains supported at its current HTTP

+review_trigger: operational signal fields, collection destination or privacy policy changes
+# Keep operational observations separate from calculation values
+Cooper agreed on 10 October 2026 to allow only safe operational details in the
+Axiom and Cloudflare logging and metrics design: fixed fields such as stage,
+route, duration and safe error name. Salaries, calculation facts, results and
+calculation traces are excluded. This makes operational diagnosis less detailed
+but keeps financial circumstances out of the signal store.
+The policy applies to platform-generated records as well as application logs.
+URLs, request headers and raw errors need separate field-level review before
+export because they can contain financial or identifying values. The
+will propose the exact field and destination contracts. It does not authorise
+collection, provider configuration, secrets, billing or deployment. PostHog
+retains its history; its destination and collection choices are not approved by
+review_trigger: public browser access, publication address or remote MCP origin policy changes
+# Public browser API and Production publication links
+On 13 October 2026 Cooper chose Common Practice's public, credential-free
+browser API policy and fixed Production publication links. Pages and discovery
+documents name `https://taxkit.dev`, including in Preview; API endpoint entries
+still name their actual stage's API. Each host keeps its own native address,
+and Website receives the API address/binding without a reverse dependency.
+This makes publication links consistent and removes the circular deployment
+graph, at the cost of replacing stage-specific publication links.
+Remote MCP has a separate native policy: Origin-less desktop/server clients
+remain supported, and the initial browser list is `https://taxkit.dev`. Add
+other browser sites only for a known need. No Effect predicate patch is selected.
+TaxKit's on-page tools remain independent of that remote endpoint policy.
+owns the migration, including caller/rate/body/work checks and safe errors.
+This records the agreed design; it does not claim deployed behaviour.

<result>I mapped the API side end to end. Two items you asked about do not exist in this worktree: there is no `ALCHEMY_PHASE` check, and the API sets no `Cache-Control` headers. Paths below are relative to the worktree root.

## 1. apps/api (Cloudflare Worker)

**Entry and how it is built**
- **`apps/api/src/worker.ts`**
  - :87-95 declares `class TaxKitApiWorker extends Worker<…, { fetch: HttpEffect; calculatorRequest: … }>()("TaxKitApi")`.
  - :101-113 is the default export: `TaxKitApiWorker.make({ compatibility 2026-10-04 + nodejs_compat, env: { API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Worker.URL }, observability: ApiWorkerObservability (all off, :25-35), workersDev: true }, ApiWorkerNativeInit)`.
- **Service layer order (:37-51):** `PublicCalculatorServiceLive` → `PublicCalculatorServiceRateLimited` → `PublicCalculatorServiceBounded` (+ `CalculationEngineLive`) → `ApiCalculatorAnalyticsLive`, merged with `ApiContentLive`.
- **`ApiWorkerNativeInit` (:79-85)** adds `McpSessionHostLive`, `ApiAnalyticsLive` (PostHog via `FetchHttpClient`/`NodeCrypto`) and `ApiCalculatorAdmission` with `RateLimitBinding`. `TaxKitApiBinding` is at :97-99.
- **`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts`** (`ApiWorkerApplication`, :57):
  - Settings are read lazily with `Effect.cached(ApiWorkerSettingsConfig)` (:61), so origins resolve on first request, not during planning.
  - Routes (:111-117) are `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer` (built with `HttpApiBuilder.layer(TaxKitApi)` in `packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts:17`) merged with `TaxKitRpcHttpLayer`. They are given content/discovery and use `HttpRouter.provideRequest(calculator)`. `HttpRouter.toHttpEffect(routes)` is at :118.
  - `fetch` (:159-211) is wrapped in `safeHttpEffect` from `alchemy/Http`. That function catches causes, returns 499 for interrupt-only and 500 otherwise. A `ConfigError` returns 503 (:207-209).
  - The public `fetch` (:277-284) gets its rate key from `calculatorEdgeRateKey(headers)`, falling back to `localKey`. `localKey` is 127.0.0.1 only when `CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE=local-emulator` and the API origin is http on localhost (:62-85).
- **Plan check:** nothing reads `ALCHEMY_PHASE`; grep finds it nowhere. Planning is detected instead in `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:28-34`: `const runtime = yield* CurrentRuntimeContext; if (runtime === undefined) → admitCalculation fails CalculatorAdmissionUnavailable`.

**Private `calculatorRequest` capability** (`worker.application.ts:213-276`)
- It only accepts POST /rpc:
  - a non-`Request` input returns 503 (:218-224);
  - `request.method !== "POST" || pathname !== "/rpc"` returns 404 (:225-230).
- The rate key is decoded from the separate `encodedKey` argument (:231-233). The request then goes through the shared `fetch`.
- The reply is buffered: a byte-counting `Stream.mapAccumEffect` fails with `CalculatorRpcResponseTooLarge` above `CalculatorRpcResponseLimit` (2 MiB), followed by `Effect.timeoutOption(CalculatorRpcDeadline)` (10s) (:243-260).
- The `catchCause` site is :270: `Effect.catchCause(() => Effect.succeed(Option.none<Response>()))`, then `Option.getOrElse(… 503)` (:272-275). This also swallows interrupts.
- **Possible gap:** the 10s timeout wraps only the body-buffering stream. The `fetch` call at :234 runs before it.
- Caller: `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:50-69` (`toRpcAsync(...).calculatorRequest(incoming, formatIp(key))`). The binding is checked in `apps/web/src/lib/config.server.ts:11-20`.

**Bounded buffers**
| Limit | Location |
|---|---|
| Request body 64 KiB / 5s, POST only; 413 on size, 408 on deadline, plus a post-read clock check | `packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-34, 39-123` (re-exported via `api-rpc/request-boundary` and `apps/api/src/worker-request.boundary.ts:1`); applied at `worker.application.ts:186` |
| RPC response 2 MiB / 10s | `packages/api/rpc/src/schemas.ts:60-61` |
| MCP response 2 MiB / 10s | `apps/api/src/mcp.schemas.ts:4-5` |
| Calculator work 5s budget; concurrency 8 (semaphore `withPermitsIfAvailable`, `CalculatorCapacityExceeded` when full) | `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-10, 14-34, 42-56` |
| RPC ingress: ≤16 envelopes, ≤32 headers, ≤64 KiB | `packages/api/rpc/src/server-serialization.boundary.ts:19-60` |

**`catchCause` sites**
- `worker.application.ts:270`, described above.
- `apps/api/src/mcp-response.boundary.ts:42-48`: `timeoutOption(McpResponseDeadline)` wraps the handler and the buffering, then `catchCause((cause) => Cause.hasInterrupts(cause) ? Effect.interrupt : Effect.succeedNone)`, so failures become 503.
- Others: `apps/api/scripts/smoke-public-routes.runtime.ts:341` and `packages/api/http/src/client/server.layer.ts:27`.

**ErrorReporter**
- The API never calls `ErrorReporter.report`.
- `packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts:14-25`: `ErrorReporter.make` logs the fixed message "Calculation host failure" with `Cause.empty`, as JSON event `api.runtime.event`. It is wired through `apps/api/src/worker-telemetry.layer.ts:3` (`CalculatorHostTelemetryLive("api")`) and provided at `worker.application.ts:86, 119, 145, 211, 276`.
- Explicit `report` calls exist only in `apps/web/src/server.ts:265-268` and `apps/web/src/lib/loaders.server.ts:43-147`.

**CORS** (`worker.application.ts:189-204`)
- Uses `HttpMiddleware.cors`.
- `allowedOrigins: (origin) => origin === config.websiteOrigin.origin`, `allowedMethods: ["GET","POST","OPTIONS"]`, `credentials: false`.
- Headers: `["content-type", CollectionPolicyHeader]`. For /mcp it adds `mcp-method`, `mcp-name`, `mcp-protocol-version` and `mcp-session-id`.
- `traceparent` is not allowed. Tracing is disabled instead, which keeps it off requests:
  - server: `RpcServer.layerHttp({ disableTracing: true, protocol: "http", path: "/rpc" })` (`packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`);
  - clients: `RpcClient.make(..., { disableTracing: true })` plus `TracerDisabledWhen → true` and `RequestInit { credentials: "omit", redirect: "error" }` (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:66-72`; `content.live.layer.ts:60-66`).

**MCP**
- **Modern:** `TaxKitMcpHttpLayer(websiteOrigin, protocol = McpProtocol.v2026_07_28)` uses `McpServer.layerHttp({ allowedOrigins: [websiteOrigin.origin], path: "/mcp", name: "TaxKit", version: "1" })` (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:209-224`). It has 6 tools (:24-90), and each handler is wrapped in `withMcpRequestCancellation` (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts`, an AbortSignal race).
  - It is built once with `Effect.cached` in the instance `Scope`, with request-scoped services omitted (`worker.application.ts:126-157`).
- **Legacy:** chosen when the session host exists and `mcp-protocol-version` is absent or `2025-11-25` (`worker.application.ts:164-176`). It routes to the Durable Object `TaxKitMcpSessions` via `getByName("legacy-mcp-v2025-11-25")`. The trusted key travels in header `x-taxkit-mcp-calculator-key`; any incoming copy is stripped first (`apps/api/src/mcp-session.layer.ts:62, 277-291`).
- **Early protection in the DO fetch:** path ≠ /mcp → 404; bad Origin → 403 *before* state allocation (:158-165); malformed session id → 404; non-POST → 405. An expired or unknown id cannot create a host (:200-203). Each host allows 32 initialisations, then 429 with `retry-after` (:212-236). Requests are capped at 32 via a semaphore, then 503 (:131, 259-264). Sessions last 10 minutes and expire by alarm (:86-116, 132-148; constants in `mcp.schemas.ts:6-8`).

**Rate limit**
- `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:20-27`: `RateLimit("CALCULATOR_RATE_LIMIT", { namespaceId: CALCULATOR_RATE_NAMESPACE, simple: { limit: 60, period: 60 } })`, keyed by `NetAddress.formatIp(key)`.
- Applied by `PublicCalculatorServiceRateLimited` (`packages/calculators/src/admission.layer.ts:12-33`); a missing key gives `CalculatorAdmissionUnavailable`.
- HTTP 429 carries `retry-after: "60"` (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:76-89`).

**Cache-Control:** none is set anywhere in `apps/api/src` or `packages/{api,content,calculators}/src`. The only headers set are the `retry-after` ones above. Cache headers live in the Website:
- `apps/web/src/server.ts:103` sets `"public, max-age=300"` on discovery documents;
- `"no-store"` appears at `server.ts:68,117`, `markdown.response.server.ts:52,94,119,127` (which also sets `public, max-age=300` at :103), and `relay.adapter.layer.ts:24`.

<summary>Agent "Map ceremony tooling to retire" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>The core finding is that most of this tooling only checks itself. There is one real exception: the docs catalogue build. The public docs catalogue is generated only after acceptance records and source hashes pass, and the API and web app both read that catalogue. Everything below is from reading files; I ran no scripts.

## 1. `verification` root script chain (24 steps, run in order)

| # | Script | Runs | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | check:oxlint:types | tsc on `tools/oxlint` | Real |
| 2 | check:repository-paths:types | tsc on `tools/repository-paths` | Real (small) |
| 3 | check:repository-paths | scans `git ls-files` for absolute home or checkout paths | Real hygiene check |
| 4 | check:harness-governance | `tools/governance/check.runtime.ts` | Ceremony |
| 5 | check:quality-workflow:types | tsc | Ceremony |
| 6 | check:quality-workflow | checks the shape of `quality.yml` against `controls.json` and `automation-register.json` | Ceremony |
| 7 | check:docs:types | tsc on `tools/documentation` (turbo makes it wait for the docs-content build) | Mixed |
| 8 | check:harness-foundation-epoch:types | tsc on `tools/evals` | Ceremony |
| 9 | check:docs | `tools/documentation/check.runtime.ts` | Mixed (see §4) |
| 10 | check:runbooks | `runbook-check.runtime.ts` (HGI-203/204 hashes) | Ceremony |
| 11 | check:effect-language-service | effect-tsgo diagnostics plus tsc on a 17-line `compatibility.ts` | Smoke test only; low value but not ceremony |
| 12 | check:docs-deployment:types | `tsc -p tsconfig.alchemy.json`, which covers `alchemy*.run.ts` and `packages/infrastructure/src/**` | **Real, despite the name.** Mostly duplicates infrastructure's own `check-types`, but the `alchemy*.run.ts` files are only covered here |
| 13 | check:docs-deployment-tools:types | tsc on `tools/docs-deployment` | Ceremony |
| 14 | check:docs-deployment | `tools/docs-deployment/check.runtime.ts` (about 30 receipts under `docs/evidence/deployments/**` plus `docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`) | Ceremony |
| 15 | check:docs-deployment-automation | `automation.check.runtime.ts` plus `automation-register.json` | Ceremony |
| 16 | test:docs-deployment | vitest on `tools/docs-deployment` | Ceremony |
| 17 | lint | oxlint (boundary-directive pass, then full) | Real |
| 18 | format:check | oxfmt | Real |
| 19 | test:hgi-206 | vitest on `tools/evals/hgi-206` | Ceremony |
| 20 | test:quality-workflow | vitest on `tools/quality-workflow` | Ceremony |
| 21 | knip | turbo makes it wait for the docs-content build | Real |
| 22 | knip:production | same | Real |
| 23 | check-types | turbo across workspaces | Real |
| 24 | sdk:test:browser, web:test:browser, `--filter=web check:worker-types`, web:test:native-pair | | Real |

`release:check -- --ci` is defined in `packages/scripts/src/release-readiness/schemas.ts` (`createReleaseReadinessPlan`). It runs `verification`, `test`, `build`, `docs:validate`, `sdk:check-packed-artifact`, `sdk:validate-downstream`, `api:smoke`, `web:test:native-pair` and `changeset:status`. In CI mode it writes no evidence. Running it without `--ci` reads `docs/evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json` and builds a release-attempt receipt. Note that `web:test:native-pair` runs twice: once inside `verification` and again in the plan.

The root `test` script runs `test:documentation`, `test:repository-paths`, `test:oxlint`, then `turbo run test`.

## 2. Workflows (`.github/workflows`)

- **`docs-preview.yml`, `docs-production.yml`, `docs-production-hosted-verify.yml`, `docs-preview-teardown.yml`** (18 lines each): manual-only stubs named "… (retired)" that print a recovery pointer and `exit 1`. Nothing consumes them; nothing to keep.
- **`docs-deployment-workflow-receipts.yml`** (270 lines): fires on completion of workflows named "Docs Preview Deployment", "Docs Production Deployment" and "Docs Preview Teardown". Those names no longer exist (all now end in "(retired)"), so **this workflow can never trigger**. It runs `check:docs-deployment-workflow-input`, `check:docs-deployment-workflow-run` and a Doppler fetch. Nothing to keep.
- **`quality.yml`** (86 lines, PR plus push): installs, then runs `check:quality-workflow`, a Doppler identity check, and `release:check -- --ci`. **Keep.** Only the `check:quality-workflow` step is ceremony, and `tools/quality-workflow/policy.ts` checks this file's exact step layout, so editing `quality.yml` will break that check until it is retired.

## 3. tools/

**`tools/docs-deployment`** (860K, about 17.8k lines of TS). The retired docs deployment: Doppler custody, inventory, workflow input/run/plan/proof receipts, retirement refusal, plus fixtures.
- Consumers:
  - Root `package.json`: about 20 scripts (`check:docs-deployment*`, `check:doppler-custody`, `docs:dev:cloudflare*` (which run `retirement.runtime.ts`), `test:docs-deployment`).
  - `turbo.json`: 10 `//#check:docs-deployment*` tasks.
  - The receipts workflow.
  - `knip.json` entry/project lists.
  - `oxlint.config.ts`: about 100 path entries and override blocks.
  - `tools/oxlint/portable-rules.test.ts`: lines about 612–771 and 1313–1327 require exact override entries per file, so that test must be edited.
  - `README.md` (`check:doppler-custody`).
  - `packages/infrastructure/README.md` (lines 39 and 237).
- **App-stack tests read its fixtures.** `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.test.ts` lines 335 and 365 read `tools/docs-deployment/fixtures/alchemy-beta.80/native-apps-preview.txt` and `native-apps-production.txt` as expected native-apps plan snapshots. These two files must move, for example into `packages/infrastructure`. The `alchemy-beta.64/*` fixtures and `fake-doppler*` are used only inside docs-deployment.
- No production code imports it.

**`tools/governance`** (80K). Checks `docs/verification/repository-harness-profile.json` and `critical-journeys.json`, `docs/documentation-audit/harness-foundation/{audit,accepted}-findings.json`, `docs/product-specs/harness-foundation-improvements*`, and that `package.json#scripts.verification` calls `check:harness-governance` exactly once.
- Consumers: `verification` step 4, `test:harness-governance`, `check:harness-governance:types`, turbo task, the oxlint runtime allow-list plus `portable-rules.test.ts`.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/evals`** (176K): the `hgi-206/` and `harness-foundation/` checkers plus `hgi-206-*.json` and `harness-foundation-*.json`. They read `docs/documentation-audit/{hgi-206,harness-foundation}/**` receipts, epoch candidates and `HFI-004-candidate-*`.
- Consumers: `check:hgi-206`, `test:hgi-206` (in `verification`), `check:harness-foundation-epoch`, `check:harness-foundation-epoch:types` (in `verification`), oxlint config plus `portable-rules.test.ts`.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/quality-workflow`** (132K): policy over the shape of `quality.yml`, `controls.json`, `automation-register.json` and its fixtures. It references `packages/scripts/src/release-readiness/*` as a control owner.
- Consumers: `quality.yml` step, `verification` steps 5, 6 and 20, `knip.json`, oxlint.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/repository-paths`** (32K): rejects machine-specific absolute paths in tracked files. **A real check; worth keeping.**

**`tools/effect-language-service`** (8K): one trivial file used to smoke-test the effect-tsgo plugin (`verification` step 11, `knip.json` entry). Low value but harmless.

**`tools/documentation`**, split by usefulness:
- **Useful checks:** `policy.ts` and `check.runtime.ts` invariants `maintainer-metadata`, `lifecycle-successor`, `relative-link`, `local-bun-command` (a `bun run X` in docs must exist as a script), `workspace-readme`, `generated-source-owner`.
- **Ceremony inside the same files:**
  - The `owner-policy` invariant: requires one acceptance-record binding per published page and verifies `sourceSha256` through `verifyAcceptedSource`.
  - `DocumentationReceipt` with its nonClaim/postcondition fields.
  - The report written to `tmp/docs-policy-report.json`.
- **`owner-policy.json`** (319 lines) is mixed. Path classes (public, maintainer and sdkDocs roots, fumadocs, openApi bindings) are useful. `public.statusDecision.acceptanceRecords[]`, which maps each MDX page and `navigation.json` to `docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/public-content-acceptance/2026-10-0{6,7,8}/*.json` (284K), is ceremony.
- **Pure ceremony:**
  - `runbook-contract.json` (HGI-204).
  - `runbook-policy.ts`, which imports types from `@taxkit/scripts/release-readiness`. This is the only code import of `@taxkit/scripts` anywhere.
  - `runbook-check.runtime.ts`, which hashes the `HGI-203-*` evidence and reads `docs/runbooks/*` and `docs/operations/authority-model.md`.
- **`catalogue.build.ts`, `catalogue.runtime.ts`, `catalogue.policy.ts`: needed for the real build** (see §4).

## 4. Docs packages

**`packages/docs-content`.**
- `generate` runs `fumadocs-mdx` and `src/catalogue-index.runtime.ts`. No ceremony.
- **`build` runs `generate` and then `tools/documentation/catalogue.runtime.ts`**, which:
  1. reads the acceptance bindings in `owner-policy.json`;
  2. decodes each `PublicPageAcceptanceRecordV2`;
  3. compares SHA-256 hashes of each MDX file and `navigation.json` against the record's `sourceSha256`;
  4. calls `projectPublicCatalogue`, which requires exactly one record per page with `status: "published"` plus navigation, else fails;
  5. re-checks the hashes, then writes `.source/public-catalogue.json`.
- The build therefore **depends on acceptance records and source hashes**.
- `turbo.json` `@taxkit/docs-content#build` lists `tools/documentation/catalogue.*`, `schemas.ts`, `owner-policy.json` and the `public-content-acceptance/**/*.json` files as inputs.
- **Consumers that must keep working:**
  - `apps/api/src/content.boundary.ts` imports `@taxkit/docs-content/public-catalogue`.
  - `apps/web/scripts/docs-images.build.ts` reads it.
  - `apps/web/test/native-pair.boundary.test.ts` (line 408) reads it.
  - `knip` and `check:docs:types` wait on this build.
  - The root `docs:catalogue` script.
- **Implication:** retiring acceptance records means rewriting catalogue build/policy to filter on frontmatter `status: published` alone. The projection logic (published filter, navigation pruning, parent/child check) is worth keeping.
- `docs:validate` (`src/validate.runtime.ts`, `src/validation/*`: MDX component policy and checked snippets) is real content validation. Keep it.

**`packages/docs-fumadocs`**: no acceptance, receipt or hash code. Nothing to retire.

**`packages/content/src/schemas.ts` lines 233–261**: `PublicPageAcceptanceRecordV1`/`V2`, `DocsAcceptedSourceDigest` and the `PublicPageAcceptanceRecord` union.
- Consumers: `tools/documentation/{schemas,catalogue.build,catalogue.policy}.ts` and their tests, and `packages/content/test/schemas.test.ts` (lines 88–96).
- No app imports them.

## 5. `packages/scripts` (release-readiness, 3.8k lines)

- `release:check` runs `release-readiness.runtime.ts`. `release:present` runs `present.runtime.ts`, which reads and verifies a release-attempt receipt.
- Consumers:
  - Root scripts `release:check`, `release:present`, `test:release-readiness`.

# Product specs

This is the SPEC inventory and admission route. Current implementation intent
requires a genuinely active SPEC/task and an entry in
[`../exec-plans/active/README.md`](../exec-plans/active/README.md). Implemented,
superseded, and historical specs remain reachable for provenance but are not
default current context. See [`../README.md`](../README.md) for lifecycle.

| Spec | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [2025–26 annual Medicare correction](./medicare-2025-26-correction.md) | Implemented locally | MCR-001 and MCR-002 are completed with [correction evidence](../documentation-audit/medicare-2025-26-correction.json). The draft PR and exact approved adad source remain separate from adad qualification and deployment. |
| [Clean slate website and API foundation](./clean-slate-foundation.md) | In progress | Q1–Q13 settled: native website RPC, explicit Calculate, expandable existing explanation, calculator-first homepage and public-only Markdown. The complete 0.6.0 skill baseline and Cooper's immutable/declarative Effect policy require actual enforcement qualification. [Ordered tasks](./clean-slate-foundation.tasks.json) include retained tax behaviour, current qualified packages, enforceable rules, agent/discovery support, Alchemy DNS/Doppler, minimal PostHog and shared Axiom signals. Cooper authorised implementation on 4 October. The active plan records retained work and verification; provider-plan approval remains separate. |
| [Entire AI work history](./entire-session-history.md) | Implemented | Both agents recorded fresh sessions linked to a normal commit and push; 742 past turns imported. [Dated proof](../documentation-audit/entire-session-history/2026-10-01.json) and [draft PR #84](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/84) retain the public Sydney setup. |
| [Alchemy and Doppler modernisation](./alchemy-doppler-modernisation.md) | Implemented | The one-resource owner, beta.79/Effect upgrade and fixed Doppler contract are merged. [PR #86](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/86) closed the hosted browser-check recovery; [read-only Production check `37096642146`](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/actions/runs/37096642146) passed on merged `main`. The [completed plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-doppler-modernisation.md) and [task ledger](./alchemy-doppler-modernisation.tasks.json) retain the failed original run and proof limits. |
| [Oxlint policy refresh](./oxlint-policy-refresh.md) | Implemented | The generic and Effect anti-slop policy, portable mutable-test-state rule and structural finding fixes are implemented. Candidate `48384d5` passed hosted Quality run `33375644482`; [PR #76](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/76) merged it as `1a0b180`, and main Quality run `33376169245` passed on that merge. No package publication or deployment was performed. |
| [Doppler configuration governance](./doppler-configuration-governance.md) | Implemented | The reviewed slices, TaxKit-only bootstrap, merged-main Quality and exact absent-stage teardown are proved. The hard cutover removed direct GitHub values and eight old Cloudflare tokens. Hosted fork, served Preview and Production/rollback remain explicit non-claims. |
| [Alchemy deployment structure corrections](./alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md) | Implemented | Findings `ALC-AUD-001` through `ALC-AUD-005` and decisions `ALC-AUD-R001` through `ALC-AUD-R003` are closed. [PR #71](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/71) merged the verified candidate as `28ed00f`; the [completed plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md) retains ordered delivery and claim-matched proof. |
| [Native Alchemy docs hard cutover](./native-alchemy-hard-cutover.md) | Implemented | Native-only source/workflow admission, beta.64 sibling memo coverage and the exact Preview/teardown lock are implemented. The separately authorised five-stage Preview state reconciliation and zero-legacy final inventory are recorded in [`legacy-state-cutover.json`](../evidence/deployments/2026-08-21-native-alchemy-hard-cutover/legacy-state-cutover.json); Production was not deployed or cut over by that operation. |
| [Automatic Preview Teardown Admission](./automatic-preview-teardown-admission.md) | Implemented | PR-close teardown now shares the unreviewed Preview credential environment. Corrected run `32367035323` and reconciliation `32367125582` proved the automatic exact-stage no-op path; the old approval environment is removed and Production remains protected. |
| [Shared Dependency Cache and Checkout Upgrade](./shared-dependency-cache-and-checkout.md) | Implemented | PR #59 run `32357219491` passed twice on the same source commit; attempt 2 restored both exact shared keys, kept live installs and completed in 54 seconds with checkout v7.0.1. Cross-ref restore from `main` remains a post-merge proof boundary. |
| [Pull-request Turbo Write-through Cache](./pull-request-turbo-write-through.md) | Implemented | PWC-001 enables Vercel Remote Cache writes for token-bearing same-repository pull requests. Exact run `32351432522` proved a pull-request miss/write and same-commit remote hit; fork fallback and live frozen install remain. |
| [Turbo and CI Cache Efficiency](./ci-cache-efficiency.md) | Implemented | TCC-001 through TCC-005 retain event-safe Vercel task caching plus separate Bun-package and Chromium caches. Same-commit hosted proof records a 79% Turbo worker saving; dependency savings remain step-bounded, and trusted Preview plan-only proof retained live authority boundaries. |
| [Quality Trigger Efficiency](./quality-trigger-efficiency.md) | Implemented | Candidate `1b45489` passed hosted Quality run `32315275636`; feature-branch push duplication is removed while pull-request and main-branch coverage remains. |
| [Native Alchemy docs deployment](./native-alchemy-docs-deployment.md) | Implemented | Candidate `7a23bf3` passed exact Git, Preview, Production, public-journey and named-stage teardown proof; future changes require a successor SPEC. |
| [Native Alchemy docs integration](./native-alchemy-docs-integration.md) | Implemented | The manual docs build/Worker graph is replaced by beta.64's first-class Website.Vite lifecycle; current proof owns one resource and the ephemeral GitHub orphan subprocess helper is retired. |
| [Strict apps and IaC](./strict-apps-and-iac.md) | Implemented | APP-IAC-001 through APP-IAC-005 hardened docs-app runtime proof and Alchemy/Cloudflare verification and inventory boundaries; the terminal audit retains four bounded adapters without changing the deployed resource graph or external state. |
| [Docs Cloudflare and Alchemy deployment](./docs-cloudflare-alchemy-deployment.md) | Implemented | DCD-001 through DCD-005 are accepted at closeout candidate `c0cd1a9`; main-sourced Preview `pr-24`, fixed Production/rollback, report-only and exact Preview teardown absence receipts remain claim-matched (`31338052297`, `31343392260`, `31343236244`, `31344401196`, `31350160353`). The completed plan retains the full history; custom-domain/DNS remains a successor non-goal. |
